doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opinions on jazz education
summary: Teaching, music lessons and being a cultured person.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I um, I took some lessons off you back in the 80s you’re a great teacher
You have a uh some opinions I’m sure you do about jazz education …
… the way it’s done, the way it should be done?

I’m all for it, I mean anything that puts an instrument in the kid’s hands is, he’s less likely to buy an Uzi and shoot me. [both chuckle] No I think I mean that I think learning an instrument makes you a better citizen, makes you no matter what you decide to do in life, I think having some music lessons and read some poetry and understand literature a little bit, speak a language. Yeah, you know, be a cultured human being. If you want to be a musician or an artist, you should be aware of ballet and classical music and literature, and you know, cinema verité, and, I mean, learn about what’s going on in the world of

culture. Um, if you just want to be a working stiff, you know, and that’s okay, you want to play with a circus band or be in the pit all your life, that’s nothing wrong with that. But I’m talking about if you’re interested in the artistry of music then you have to learn about art in general, you know. That’s an all- consuming uh study, you know.
